extracted.intended_audience: hospital quality measurement stakeholders (hospitals, measure developers, EHR vendors, CMS program staff), and public commenters
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and criteria for adopting, modifying, testing, reporting, and removing hospital electronic clinical quality measures (eCQMs) in the Hospital Inpatient Quality Reporting Program, with specific measure specifications for Hospital Harm—Postoperative VTE and several EDAC measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denominator for Hospital Harm—Postoperative VTE
rubrics_metrics.description: The denominator is the number of adult patients who had a surgical procedure performed in the operating room during an inpatient hospitalization. The cohort includes inpatient hospitalizations for patients aged 18 and older where a surgical procedure was performed inside the operating room during the encounter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denominator excludes inpatient encounters for: patients with an obstetric-related diagnosis; a VTE diagnosis present on admission; acute brain or spinal injury or hemorrhage present on admission; extracorporeal membrane oxygenation during the inpatient encounter; a thrombectomy procedure before or on the same day as the first surgical procedure; intracranial or spinal surgery where the patient was discharged less than five days after the end of the surgery; and inpatient encounters with a duration of stay less than 2 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk adjustment for Hospital Harm—Postoperative VTE
rubrics_metrics.description: The risk adjustment model accounts for factors that affect risk of VTE, specifically age, sex, and eight clinical factors (bleeding disorders, cancer, catheter insertion, history of VTE, obesity, respiratory operations, stroke, and vascular surgeries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model developed using two consecutive years (CY 2022–2023) of EHR data from a commercial EHR database. Testing demonstrated discrimination between high- and low-risk events and high reliability; the model was designed to ensure hospitals caring for higher-risk patients are evaluated fairly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerator definition for Hospital Harm—Postoperative VTE
rubrics_metrics.description: A qualifying postoperative VTE requires documentation of both an imaging procedure to diagnose the VTE and initiation of anticoagulant therapy within 24 hours of the imaging procedure, with the anticoagulant provided at a dose consistent with therapeutic treatment of VTE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The conjunction of (a) diagnostic imaging, (b) anticoagulant within 24 hours, and (c) therapeutic dosing minimizes misclassification between treatment and prophylaxis/maintenance therapy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure testing and validation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures must be tested for feasibility, reliability, and validity using appropriate data samples and methods (e.g., multi-year EHR data, hospital samples, clinical adjudication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example testing described: sample of 100,911 hospitalizations from 34 hospitals across six states (CY 2022–2023); signal-to-noise reliability scores reported; data element validity testing against chart abstraction showed strong agreement for most elements, moderate to excellent sensitivity/specificity for numerator/denominator, and moderate-to-low sensitivity for certain denominator exclusions (possibly site-specific). Testing should include multiple EHR systems to ensure generalizability.

rubrics_metrics.name: EHR system testing / technical implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure feasibility and technical implementation must be evaluated across the EHR systems commonly in use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Testing sites included Epic, Allscripts, Cerner, and Meditech. CMS acknowledges potential bias where single enterprise-wide EHRs capture more post-discharge events; systems with multiple EHRs may capture fewer events. Ongoing monitoring and routine measure maintenance are expected to identify technical implementation issues and unintended consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a 30-day post-discharge window
rubrics_metrics.description: A 30-day post-discharge timeframe is the proposed window for assessing postoperative VTE and other adverse events related to a hospital admission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justification: 30 days is common among related measures; evidence shows roughly one third of VTEs occur between postoperative day 14 and end of fourth week. Concerns about the window (e.g., appropriateness/overlap) should be considered in public comments and testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: All-payer vs. claims-only coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Preference for all-payer eCQMs that capture care for all patients rather than measures limited to Medicare claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hospital Harm—Postoperative VTE is an all-payer eCQM (captures all patients) and could potentially replace claims-based measures like PSI 12, which capture Medicare beneficiaries only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring for unintended consequences and overuse
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopted measures should include plans for ongoing monitoring and evaluation to identify potential unintended consequences, including overtreatment (e.g., unnecessary anticoagulation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS may consider developing complementary measures (e.g., overuse of anticoagulation) in future measure development and rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data source and submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Hospital Harm—Postoperative VTE eCQM uses data collected through hospitals' EHRs and is intended to be calculated by certified health IT and submitted to CMS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All required data elements (numerator, denominator, risk adjustment) are defined in value sets available in the Value Set Authority Center (VSAC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure removal criterion — availability of better outcome measure
rubrics_metrics.description: A measure may be removed under removal factor 5 when there is availability of a measure that is more strongly associated with desired patient outcomes for the topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: proposal to remove VTE-1 and VTE-2 eCQMs if Hospital Harm—Postoperative VTE (an outcome-focused eCQM) is adopted, as the outcome measure better assesses the incidence of postoperative VTE events and aligns with reducing program burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure removal criterion — topped out performance
rubrics_metrics.description: A measure may be removed under removal factor 1 if performance among hospitals is so high and unvarying that meaningful distinctions and improvements can no longer be made (i.e., 'topped out').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational criteria include statistically indistinguishable performance at 75th and 90th percentiles and truncated coefficient of variation ≤ 0.10; consistent high reporting levels bolster the case for removal (example: STK-02).

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand cohorts to include Medicare Advantage beneficiaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Modify measures to include Medicare Advantage encounters in addition to Medicare Fee-For-Service to better reflect all Medicare beneficiaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: Medicare Advantage now comprises >50% of Medicare population; inclusion improves comprehensiveness and reliability and increases hospital result availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shorten reporting period when reliability permits
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting/performance period length can be shortened (e.g., from 3 years to 2 years) when inclusion changes (e.g., adding Medicare Advantage) achieve acceptable reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: after adding Medicare Advantage, modified EDAC measures achieved mean reliability > CBE minimum of 0.6, supporting shortening the performance period to provide more timely results.

rubrics_metrics.name: EDAC measure calculation approach (risk-standardized excess days)
rubrics_metrics.description: EDAC measures assess number of days a patient spends in acute care within 30 days post-discharge and compute hospital-level 30-day all-cause EDAC as a risk-adjusted random-effects binomial model calculating excess days per 100 discharges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model calculates difference between predicted and expected days (predicted = hospital's average adjusted; expected = average-performing hospital with same case mix). Unplanned readmissions defined using the planned readmission algorithm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'days in acute care' for EDAC
rubrics_metrics.description: Days in acute care are defined as days spent in an ED, an observation stay, or admitted as an unplanned readmission to a short-term acute care hospital within 30 days from discharge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ED visits are counted as one whole day regardless of hours or cross-date visits. Observation stays are counted by hours and rounded up to the nearest whole day.

rubrics_metrics.name: EDAC denominator inclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: To be included in the EDAC cohort, patients must: have a principal discharge diagnosis of AMI, heart failure, or pneumonia; be enrolled in Medicare FFS Part A and Part B or Medicare Advantage for 12 months prior and enrolled in Part A or Medicare Advantage during index admission; be aged 65 or older; be discharged alive from a non-federal short-term acute care hospital or Veterans Health Administration hospital; and not be transferred to another acute care facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed denominator exclusions per condition are specified in EDAC methodology reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk adjustment variables for EDAC measures
rubrics_metrics.description: EDAC measures adjust for patient age, comorbid diseases, and indicators of patient frailty (functional status) as part of case-mix adjustment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For hospital-level risk-standardization, the model includes demographics, comorbidities, severity indicators, and frailty to help account for varying patient complexities; developers empirically select index and pre-index variables based on prevalence and association with outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-rulemaking review and endorsement process expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures undergo pre-rulemaking review by Recommendation Groups and CBE endorsement processes that include voting and may result in endorsement, conditional endorsement, or non-endorsement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concerns raised by reviewers often include timeframe appropriateness (30-day window), overlap with other measures, potential unintended consequences, methodological refinements (diagnostic clarity, risk adjustment), technical implementation in EHRs, and whether the measure meaningfully advances quality. Conditions may require exploring additional risk factors (e.g., social determinants) by the next maintenance review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of hospital-level reporting effects and exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: When deciding adjustments or additions (e.g., not adjusting for rurality/medically underserved), note program-specific reporting requirements and exemptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS does not adjust EDAC for rurality or medically underserved status (consistent with other readmission measures); Critical Access Hospitals (CAHs) are not required to report to the Hospital Inpatient Quality Reporting Program, which factors into policy decisions.
